Author: Pankaj Bhatia
Bench: Pankaj Bhatia
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:165302
Court No. - 66
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 40865 of 2021
Applicant :- Shamshad

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Anurag Pandey,Ashwani Kumar Sachan,Saurabh Sachan
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned AGA and perused the record.
2. The FIR in question was lodged alleging that the daughter of the informant was married to the applicant about four months ago.
It was alleged that sufficient dowry was paid at the time of marriage, however, there always used to be a further demand of dowry.

It was also alleged that the daughter of the informant used to inform that she was being beaten up consistently and on 27.05.2018, informant was received that the daughter of the informant has been killed.

3. Learned counsel for the applicant argues that the applicant is the husband and is languishing in jail since 30.05.2018 and although, more than five years have elapsed, the trial has not concluded and there is no likelihood of the conclusion of trial in the near future in view of number of witnesses Shamshad vs State Of U.P. on 17 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32714696/
1 proposed to be examined in the charge-sheet being 27.

He draws my attention to the statement of Mohd. Salim, the informant, and the father of the informant who stated in his cross-examination that the elder daughter of the informant was married to the applicant and as the matrimonial alliance with the elder daughter did not bear any child, the second daughter of the informant was also married with the applicant with the consent of the elder daughter of the informant who had no objection to the said alliance.

In the light of the said statement in the cross-examination, it is proposed to be argued that once the informant himself has admitted that the marriage was with the consent of the elder daughter, the allegation with regard to dowry probably cannot withstand the test of judicial scrutiny.
4. Learned AGA has opposed the bail application.

5. Considering the said statement on record coupled with the fact that the applicant has suffered incarceration for a period of more than five years without any likelihood of the trial being concluded in near future, prima-facie, his rights under Article 21 of the Constitution of India have been violated.
Thus, in view of the law laid down in the case of Rabi Prakash v. The State of Odishadecided in Special Leave to Appeal (Crl.) No(s).4169 of 2023, the applicant is entitled to be enlarged on bail.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Special Leave to Appeal (Crl.) No(s).4169 of 2023
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view thereof, the application is allowed.

6. Let the applicant Shamshad be released on bail in FIR No.247 of 2018, under Section 498A, 302,
304B IPC read with Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, P.S. Bilhaur, District Kanpur nagar on his furnishing a personal bond with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
